clue.text: Relax before wet weather's in control

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes before the rain, and the wet weather is said to be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to hold them in check, a direct synonym of the verb control.

clue.text: Band initially recorded in neighbour's garage

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A band first made its recordings in the garage next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' reads as a group of musicians, fitting the garage scene, but it is a circular strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circular band, as worn on a finger or round a bird's leg.

clue.text: Sharpness of mind shown by copper getting in the last word

indicators.note: getting in means one thing goes inside another

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
amen is the word that ends a prayer

explanation.surface: A sharp-minded police officer insists on having the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or shrewdness, the quality of a quick, sharp mind.

clue.text: Drive suspect to court for jury's decision

indicators.note: suspect letters are dubious and not to be trusted in their present order

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Police take a suspect to court so a jury can decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive suspect to court' reads as transporting a suspect, but 'suspect' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the finding a jury reaches at the end of a trial.

clue.text: Outrageous tirade following drop in performance

indicators.note: following means the first-named piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: to flag is to tire and perform less well
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A manager launches into an outrageous tirade after a team's form dips.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means shockingly obvious and shameless, as in an outrageous breach of rules.

clue.text: Take steps to promote domestic order, when routine has broken down

definitions.text: Take steps to promote domestic order

indicators.note: something broken down has fallen apart, so its letters can be rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: When the household routine collapses, someone acts to restore order at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The long definition is a playful description: teaching a pet not to soil the house brings order to the home.
explanation.definitionFit: To house-train a pet is to teach it clean habits indoors, a step towards an orderly home.

clue.text: Let sap develop in parts of plant

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Allow the sap to grow through a plant's parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Petals are the coloured leaf-like segments of a flower, which is part of a plant.

clue.text: Doctor carrying oxygen about is rather inferior

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying an oxygen supply around is not up to much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of carrying something around, but it supplies its own short piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means only middling in quality, a little below standard.

clue.text: Game fellow took part in criminal activity

blocks.note: loo is an old card game
Ted is a man's name, so any fellow

explanation.surface: A willing chap joined in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' reads as willing, but it is a noun: loo is a card game. 'Fellow' standing for a man's name is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Looted means plundered or stole goods, which is one form of criminal activity.

clue.text: Zoologist agrees to provide home for animal

indicators.note: the words provide a home for the answer, which lives inside them

explanation.surface: A zoologist consents to give an animal shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, an example of an animal.

clue.text: State in which first man rejected fossil fuel used by vehicle

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the name runs the other way

blocks.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
natural gas is a fossil fuel

explanation.surface: A country where people turned against cars burning fossil fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a US state, but here it is a sovereign country; 'used by' just places the fuel beside the vehicle that burns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is an island nation off Africa, and a state in the sense of a sovereign country.

clue.text: Language understood by those in the know has primarily Japanese element

definitions.text: Language understood by those in the know

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the leading letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Insider language is said to be chiefly Japanese in content.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the specialist vocabulary of a trade or group, opaque to outsiders.

clue.text: Crazy dog kills old Charlie character in nursery story

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A mad dog kills an old Charlie in a children's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes every letter of the first two words plus the two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldilocks is the girl who visits the three bears' house in the children's tale.

clue.text: It's correct to sit back in pursuit

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction
to sit in something is to be placed inside it

explanation.surface: Someone claims it is right to lie back while being chased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct' is the verb, to punish, not the adjective; 'It's' is the opening fodder, not a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to rebuke or punish someone, the disciplinary sense of correct as a verb.

clue.text: Popular female abridged translation for Kindle

indicators.note: abridged means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
a translation renders something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular woman's shortened translation is offered on the e-reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like Amazon's e-reader, matching the translation theme, but it is the verb to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to set on fire or stir up, as kindle means to ignite.

clue.text: Setter taking one small measure from apothecary for nasty headache

indicators.note: taking means holding other material inside

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
I is the Roman numeral for one
the grain is the smallest unit of apothecaries' weight

explanation.surface: A crossword setter takes a small dose from the chemist for a bad headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' meaning the puzzle's author, hence ME, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe, recurring headache, often with nausea.

clue.text: Injures muscles in races

blocks.note: first meaning: pulls or overstretches muscles

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls muscles while running in races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races' reads as sprints, but it means breeds or varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: Strains are both muscle injuries from overstretching and distinct varieties or breeds of animals or plants.

clue.text: Lust and pain marred wedding ceremony

indicators.note: marred means spoilt or damaged, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Desire and suffering spoiled a marriage service.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a wedding and its ceremony.

clue.text: Neptune's spear found in decomposed net after turning up soil

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means read from bottom to top
decomposed means broken into its parts, so they can be reassembled
after places the piece it names behind the other one

explanation.surface: The sea god's spear is found in a rotting net dredged from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is the three-pronged spear carried by Neptune, Roman god of the sea.

clue.text: Pretend to be ill to avoid working with horribly mean girl

definitions.text: Pretend to be ill to avoid working

indicators.note: horribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A spiteful girl fakes sickness to skip work.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to feign illness to escape duty, exactly as the definition spells out.

clue.text: Recopied email to a girl

indicators.note: something recopied is written out again, here in a new order

explanation.surface: An email is copied out again and sent to a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a girl's first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Might primate get something to eat with a drink before dinner?

definitions.text: something to eat with a drink before dinner

explanation.surface: Could a monkey be given a snack with its pre-dinner drink?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' reads as the opening of a question, but it supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served with drinks before a meal.

clue.text: Arrived with artist's photographic equipment

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: Someone turned up carrying a painter's photographic kit.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for a member of the Royal Academy, is a standard crossword abbreviation for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device used to take photographs.

clue.text: Unconventional mum moaned dreadfully about teacher's last written reminder

indicators.note: last points at the closing letter of the word before it
dreadfully signals disorder, and about says the jumbled letters go round the single extra one

explanation.surface: An unusual mother complains bitterly about the note the teacher sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: All the letters are mixed together, the extra one included.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a written note serving as a reminder or record.

clue.text: Miss second sleep

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: Someone misses a second chance to nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to miss it out or not attend.

clue.text: Squatters heading for old house in part of central London

indicators.note: heading means the front, so only the first letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Squatters make for an old house in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is part of the surface reading of heading somewhere, not a separate link.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End, known for nightlife and theatres.

clue.text: Family's after wood to make barrel

indicators.note: after places the piece it names behind the other one

blocks.note: fir is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: The family is after timber to build a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A firkin is a small cask, traditionally a quarter of a barrel, used for beer.

clue.text: Norway at war, unfortunately, against thriving sea creature

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Norway, regrettably at war, fights a flourishing marine animal.
explanation.walkthrough: NARWHALE is a less common spelling of narwhal, the Arctic whale with a long tusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhale is an Arctic whale whose male has a single long spiral tusk.
